newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The racing world was rocked with the news yesterday Melbourne Cup winner Saintly has sustained a serious leg injury, sidelining the galloper for a year, and possibly his life. The 'Horse from Heaven' has bowed a tendon in one of its legs and is the third star-performer to succumb to the injury this year, with both Alpha and Portland Player out for the autumn season. Page 22.

The Australian Rugby League has refused offers from Super League defectors Jack Elsegood and John Cross to return their $150,000 loyalty agreements and play for their rebel league clubs in the opening round of the competition this weekend. Supreme Court udge David Hodgson is to hand down his judgement at 3pm today. Page 22.

Management of the Sydney Swans fear they will be forever the poor relation in New South Wales if the Australian Football League doesn't support its plan to move to the Olympic Games Stadium in Homebush. Swans chairman Richard Colless says if the club doen't get the go-ahead to play at the stadium, it could be another 50 years until it has the opportunity to play at an ultra-modern facility. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales (NSW) Rugby officials are concerned at the lack of depth they have of tight-head props in the State, playing three players out of position in the hope of solving the problem during last night's NSW A - Emerging Warratah's match at the Sydny Football Stadium. Page 46

Defending Australian Ladies Masters champion Jane Crafter has described this year's promotional slogan: "Have You Ever Been Hit By A Girl" as patronising and sexist on the eve of the championship which begins at Royal Pines on the Gold Coast today. Page 4.

Matthew Elliott further staked his claim for a test berth after top-scoring for Australia in their international match against the Transvall Invitation XI yesterday. Australia dismissed the home team for 182 after scoring 7-261 in 45 overs. Bichel and Gillespie were the best of the Australian bowlers. Page 45.
THE AGE

Carlton dispelled rumours their team is becoming too old to play competitive football as they disposed of Melbourne 13.9.(87) to 9.10.(64) in the first round of the Ansett Cup last night. The win earns them a second round tilt at either Port Fremantle or Adelaide Saturday week. Page B8.

Australian cricketer Glenn McGrath will play in the first test against South Africa this week despite suffering from a stomach virus. Team mates Greg Blewett and Jason Gillespie have also been suffering from the virus, but team Errol Alcott said there islittle doubt all three will play. Page B6.

High-flying Victorian Emma George will collect nearly A$100, 000 if she wins the pole vault and sets another world record, her 11th, at next month's world indoor championships in Paris next month. Both George and Athletics Australia are pressing Olympic fficials for women's pole vaulting to be included at the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Melbourne captain Gary Lyon took the first steps on the road to recovery last night, playing a quarter for reserves in the first round of the Ansett Cup. Lyon collected seven kicks, seven marks and one handball in his midfield role after sitting most of ast season out with a chronic back injury. Page 96.

One of Australia's most durable cyclists, Danny Clark, has announced his retirement on the international circuit after competing in 234 six-day races, 25 years after winning a silver medal at the 1972 Munich Olympic Games. Clark plans to race and coach in Australia. Page 93.

Melbourne Knights captain Andrew Marth has told club officials that they must recruit three quality players if the team hopes to climb out of its form slump its been in all season. Marth, who has been dogged by rumours that he is leaving the club, says te team desperately needs two strikers and a wide midfielder to give them any chance of making this year's finals. Page 93.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker has announced the sponsorship arrangement between the ARL and major sponsor Tooheys is up in the air, after revelations the company is going to pull out of all sport sponsorship and concentrate on mas media advertising. Page 92.

Newcastle Knights will mark their 10th year in the Australian Rugby League with a new strip, a new theme and according to captain Paul Harragon, a new attitude. Harragon believes the introduction of the Hunter Mariners in the Super League competition wil spur the Knights on from a disappointing season last year. Page 91.

Australian Federation Cup captain Lesley Bowrey is taking into account Durban's intense humidity when she picks the team for the up-coming tie against South Africa this weekend. Rachel McQuillan and Annabel Ellwood appear the likely singles players, but owrey must decide whether one of them can back up in the doubles match. Page 87.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
